AI Weekly Digest
July 07, 2026
A few things worth knowing this week — here's what's happening in AI, in plain English.
TL;DR — Top picks this week
If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
Google has changed its privacy settings so it can keep more of the data you upload—such as photos, files, and audio or video recordings—to train its artificial‑intelligence tools. If you use Google for work, this means some of your company information could be used for that purpose unless you choose to opt out. The article explains how to turn the setting off.
The browser wars aren’t about search anymore — here are the best alternatives to Chrome and Safari
A new guide lists several web browsers that aim to compete with Chrome and Safari. These alternatives may offer different features, such as stronger privacy or faster performance. Trying a different browser could improve the way you browse the web for work tasks.
Savi’s app aims to protect consumers from realistic AI scams like kidnappers demanding ransom
Savi has built an app that alerts users when they receive AI‑created scams, such as fake ransom threats. The company just secured $7 million in seed funding and will launch the app for iPhone and Android on Tuesday. Using this tool could help protect our team from fraud attempts that look increasingly realistic.
🛠️ Tools & Products
The browser wars aren’t about search anymore — here are the best alternatives to Chrome and Safari
A new guide lists several web browsers that aim to compete with Chrome and Safari. These alternatives may offer different features, such as stronger privacy or faster performance. Trying a different browser could improve the way you browse the web for work tasks.
Read more →
Savi’s app aims to protect consumers from realistic AI scams like kidnappers demanding ransom
Savi has built an app that alerts users when they receive AI‑created scams, such as fake ransom threats. The company just secured $7 million in seed funding and will launch the app for iPhone and Android on Tuesday. Using this tool could help protect our team from fraud attempts that look increasingly realistic.
Read more →
Money Magician – AI financial co-pilot for founders (not a budgeting app)
Money Magician is an AI‑powered helper that works with company founders to give quick financial insights and advice, not just a simple budgeting tool. It could make it easier for our leadership to understand cash flow, plan spending, and spot financial risks without needing a finance expert on hand.
Read more →
🏢 Industry & Adoption
The only AI glossary you’ll need this year
A new glossary collects the most common artificial‑intelligence terms and explains them in plain language. It’s designed to help anyone keep up with the buzzwords you might hear in meetings or training. Having a quick reference can make it easier for us to understand AI projects and discussions.
Read more →
The foundational elements of AI architecture that IT leaders need to scale
The article explains the basic building blocks that IT teams should focus on when expanding the use of AI across the company. Understanding these foundations helps us invest in the right technology now so our AI projects can grow smoothly in the future.
Read more →
Air Con in a Warming Climate
This piece looks at how rising temperatures are making air‑conditioning needs more demanding and costly for businesses. It matters to us because higher cooling demand can increase energy bills and affect the comfort of our office spaces.
Read more →
Ford rehired engineers it replaced with AI – the real reason is worse
Ford has decided to bring back engineers it previously let go in favor of AI tools. This suggests that relying solely on AI for complex work may not be reliable, a lesson we might keep in mind when considering automation in our own processes.
Read more →
Microsoft is laying off 4,800 employees
Microsoft announced it is laying off about 4,800 workers, mostly in its sales and Xbox divisions, adding to cuts it made last year. This could affect the availability of Microsoft products and support we rely on, and it signals broader industry hiring trends that may impact our own planning.
Read more →
🔬 Research
Coaxing quality (writing) output from generative AI
The write‑up shares tips on how to get clearer, more useful writing from AI text generators. Applying these ideas could help our teams produce better emails, reports, and marketing copy without spending as much time editing.
Read more →
🛡️ Safety & Policy
If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
Google has changed its privacy settings so it can keep more of the data you upload—such as photos, files, and audio or video recordings—to train its artificial‑intelligence tools. If you use Google for work, this means some of your company information could be used for that purpose unless you choose to opt out. The article explains how to turn the setting off.
Read more →
Bank of England sees growing risks to financial stability from AI
The Bank of England has warned that artificial‑intelligence technology could create new risks to the stability of the financial system. Such risks might affect interest rates, lending practices, or the overall economy. Keeping an eye on this warning can help our finance team anticipate possible market changes.
Read more →
The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
A recent ransomware attack used an AI program to carry out the technical steps of the breach, while a person still chose the target and provided the stolen login details. This shows that AI can be weaponized by attackers, so we need to be extra vigilant about our cybersecurity defenses.
Read more →
